description:
Look an Interslavic word up in the bundled community dictionary and return
its translation matrix (English + 11 Slavic languages) plus its full,
algorithmically-generated declension/conjugation table. Any form and either
script works; an inflected query resolves to its headword and the result notes
it. With search_language='eng' the query is an English word: the result lists
its Interslavic equivalents plus their expanded entries. Returns Markdown plus
the same result as structuredContent matching the declared outputSchema.

Fully offline (bundled snapshot); calls are rate limited per client IP.
Content: the Interslavic dictionary (van Steenbergen et al.); reuse licence
unconfirmed — attribute the source.

SearchLanguage.description:
The query language. ``isv`` looks an Interslavic word up directly — any of its
inflected forms resolves to the headword via the bundled reverse form index, and
a Latin or Cyrillic spelling both work. ``eng`` searches in reverse: the English
query is matched against the entries' English glosses and each matched Interslavic
lemma is then looked up normally. The dictionary translates into 11 more Slavic
languages, but only isv and eng are QUERYABLE in v1 — the other columns are
read-only (returned in each entry's translation matrix).
SearchLanguage.title: SearchLanguage

include_forms.description: When true (default), each match's full declension/conjugation table is returned INLINE — usable cases/tenses in ONE call, no follow-up interslavic_get_inflections. Set false for a cheap screen of which entries exist. Bounded by a per-search cap — use max_forms to adjust per call. Pronouns, numerals and indeclinables carry no table. For eng queries this governs the expanded Interslavic entries.
include_forms.title: Include Forms

max_forms.description: Optional override for how many inflection tables to expand this call (0–12). Tables are served from the bundled dataset (no network), so this is cheap. Omit for the server default.
max_forms.title: Max Forms

query.description: The word to look up, in the language search_language names. Interslavic (default): a SINGLE Interslavic word, any form and either script — an inflected form ('brata') resolves to its headword ('brat') via the reverse form index, Latin and Cyrillic both work for headwords, and diacritics are optional ('delati' finds 'dělati'). English (search_language='eng'): the English word whose Interslavic equivalents you want.
query.title: Query

search_language.description: Language the query is in: 'isv' (default) looks the Interslavic word up directly; 'eng' finds the Interslavic equivalents of an English word (via the gloss index) and returns their full entries. These are the only two queryable languages in v1 — each entry ALSO carries a read-only translation matrix into 11 more languages (Russian, Polish, Czech, Ukrainian, …), but you cannot query IN those.

name: interslavic_search

AdjectiveParadigm.description:
Declension of an adjective: singular and plural case tables (each case key →
the gender forms the engine renders, [masculine, neuter, feminine] where the case
distinguishes all three, fewer where it collapses them), the ``short`` form, and
the ``comparison`` degrees (positive/comparative/superlative).

entry_id.description: The dictionary word id (NOT the headword).
entry_id.title: Entry Id

short.description: The short (predicative) form; may be empty.
short.title: Short

source.default: Interslavic dictionary (Medžuslovjansky slovnik), J. van Steenbergen et al. — steen.free.fr / medzuslovjansky (interslavic-dictionary.com). Morphology by @interslavic/utils. Reuse licence unconfirmed; reused here with attribution.
source.title: Source

AdjectiveParadigm.title: AdjectiveParadigm

Entry.description:
One Interslavic dictionary entry: the headword (in both scripts), its part of
speech, and its translation matrix — the entry's content. ``word_class`` is the
paradigm class ('noun'/'adjective'/'verb') or '' when the word has no generated
table; feed ``entry_id`` + ``word_class`` to ``interslavic_get_inflections``.

intelligibility.description: Per-language intelligibility flags as the source marks them.
intelligibility.title: Intelligibility

Entry.title: Entry

InflectionHandle.description:
A structured anchor for fetching a full paradigm: feed ``entry_id`` (the word
id) + ``word_class`` (the paradigm class) to ``interslavic_get_inflections`` — or
ask ``search`` to include the table inline (``forms``).

entry_id.description: The dictionary word id — NOT the headword.
entry_id.title: Entry Id

forms.description: The full paradigm, populated when a search is asked to include forms. None when not requested or beyond the cap.
forms.title: Forms

InflectionHandle.title: InflectionHandle

NounParadigm.description:
Declension of a noun: case key → [singular, plural]. Interslavic has one
number split (sg/pl) across seven cases. A cell may hold ' / '-separated
alternates exactly as the reference engine renders them; a number the paradigm
doesn't fill is an empty string. ``category`` discriminates the ``Forms`` union —
switch on it before reading the body.

cases.description: Case key ('nom','acc','gen','loc','dat','ins','voc') → [singular, plural], in table order.
cases.title: Cases

entry_id.description: The dictionary word id (NOT the headword).
entry_id.title: Entry Id

source.default: Interslavic dictionary (Medžuslovjansky slovnik), J. van Steenbergen et al. — steen.free.fr / medzuslovjansky (interslavic-dictionary.com). Morphology by @interslavic/utils. Reuse licence unconfirmed; reused here with attribution.
source.title: Source

ParadigmNotFound.description:
No inflection table for this word/class: an indeclinable (adverb, preposition,
conjunction, …), a multiword lemma, or a pronoun/numeral (closed sets carry no
generated table in v1). ``found`` is False and there is no body.

TranslationMatrix.description:
One entry's translations into the dictionary's target languages (isv → …).
An absent translation is an empty string. English (``en``) is also the reverse
search key; the Slavic columns are read-only in v1. This IS the entry's content —
Interslavic is a bridge language, so the multilingual equivalents are the point.
TranslationMatrix.title: TranslationMatrix

TranslationSense.title: TranslationSense

TranslationTerm.description:
One Interslavic word an English query's gloss match offers. ``word`` is the
headword (what an ``eng`` search re-searches and what a handle needs).
TranslationTerm.title: TranslationTerm

VerbParadigm.description:
Conjugation of a verb: the finite tense/mood series (each a positional list of
person forms — see the grammar-labels resource for the person order per series),
the imperative, the participles (present/past × active/passive, present only when
the aspect licenses them) and the verbal noun (gerund). Alternates are
comma-separated as the reference engine renders them.
